newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Gold in range, silver to stabilise lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Gold in range, silver to stabilise lower.

text.p: Gold is expected to range-trade on Thursday between $316.50 and $322, ahead of a test of last week's low of $313.60, dealers and analysts said.
Silver would try to stabilise after testing new lower ground, they added.
GOLD -
On an intra-day basis, the market is expected to remain in a price band similar to Wednesday's, but a break lower could come soon, traders said.
"In the medium term I am not convinced that it is all over. It could come tomorrow, or next week, it's hard to say," said a dealer in continental Europe.
Australian producer buy-backs underpinned the market on Wednesday, which touched a high of $321.25, but investment funds entered the market again to send prices to a low bid of $316.40, traders said.
The declining 10-day moving average could help weigh down the market, which was at $320 at the New York close on Wednesday and about $1 lower early on Thursday.
Support should be seen at Wednesday's low around $316.50, then at $315.00, with the key floor at the 12-year low of $313.60 hit last week.
At 0810 GMT spot gold was quoted at $318.40/318.90 up 60 cents from Wednesday's New York close.
SILVER -
The market was under the influence of gold, succumbing to lower numbers on Wednesday, ending in New York at $4.21/$4.23.
In early activity on Thursday, spot prices lurched down to $4.12/$4.14.
"It should be much higher from the fundamentals, but it can't act independently of gold for the time being," said the European dealer.
Prices were expected to attempt to stabilise later on Thursday, but not a lot of support was under the market.

On the Comex September contract, a move above 427/427.5 cents would be a signal that an upward correction of the previous month's 70-cent slide was underway, Elliott Wave International said in report.
At 0810 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.20/4.22, up one cent from Wednesday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
Prices broke above the 10-day moving average at $405. on Wednesday, which may herald a correction higher, analysts said.
Resistance is pegged at $410, the high of July 8 and 11, then at $420.
Support would be seen at the recent low around $394.

The market noted a report from Tokyo quoting local traders who said Russia's platinum group metal (PGM) export agency Almazjuvelirexport informed Japanese buyers that it would resume platinum exports next week.
The Russian agency recently resumed its palladium exports to Japan, but platinum shipments had been delayed.
At 0810 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $406.00/410.00, down 50 cents from Wednesday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
